content: RRF/weight tuning overfitting: hand-tuned fusion weights beat RRF on the tuning queries and collapse on held-out (measured: alpha-tuned recall@10 0.91 tuned vs 0.68 held-out; untuned RRF 0.85/0.79). A one-parameter model overfit to 20 points is still overfit; if you cannot hold out 30+ labeled queries you cannot afford to tune weights. Qdrant tuning guide: settle RRF k BEFORE weights (weight pair valid only for the k tested); k should track relevant-docs-per-query (k=2-5 for ~1 relevant doc, 20-61 for tens); on SciFact 300 queries no config had 95% bootstrap CI excluding zero; selected fusion kept only 67-95% of gain on held-out across 200 splits; keeping the default is a real answer. Eval set minimum 50-200 queries; re-tune after corpus shifts; a 2-point gain on 20 queries can be one case; when a reranker follows fusion, optimize recall@initial-K not precision; always pair quality metrics with latency p95. Sources: qdrant search-tuning guide, chicong115.com 2029-09 case study, claude-dev-suite alpha-tuning, testland hybrid eval skill, qaskills 2026-08.
